title: AI & Market Intelligence Briefing
headline: AI’s week blended faster, cheaper models and agent platforms with mounting legal/regulatory pressure that is starting to carry real enforcement timelines.

items.text: Google shipped three new Gemini models (including Gemini 3.6 Flash and two 3.5 Flash variants) aimed at efficiency and specialized use-cases, while its higher-end Gemini Pro/3.5 Pro update remains delayed.
OpenAI introduced 'Presence,' an enterprise-focused product for deploying and managing real-time voice agents and chatbots with controlled access to company systems and escalation paths.

UK robotics startup Humanoid raised $152M in a Series A at a $1.35B post-money valuation, funding development, deployments, and mass manufacturing plans for its robot platform and 'KinetIQ' AI software.

A U.S. judge approved Anthropic’s $1.5B settlement of a copyright class action over training Claude on books, one of the largest known U.S. copyright settlements and an early bellwether for training-data litigation.

The EU AI Act moved into enforceable phase milestones (including chatbot disclosure rules), while Illinois signed a law mandating independent third-party safety audits for certain large AI developers and China’s dedicated AI-agent rules took effect.
